Job Description Job Title: Remodeling Handyman / Trim Carpenter
High Bridge Development is a high-end residential remodeling company specializing in additions, kitchens, bathrooms, basements, whole-home renovations, outdoor living spaces, and other...

Structural Carpentry: Erects minor structures and modifies existing structures by determining dimensions, materials, and locations of doors and windows; cuts, squares, mortises, levels, and secures sills; installs joists, studs, plates, and braces; and calculates, lays out, cuts, and installs rafters using framing squares and rafter tables to ensure proper alignment, strength, and structural integrity.

Interior Trim: Installs and finishes baseboards, base mold, toe mold, crown mold, chair rails, picture molding, and wainscoting by accurately measuring, cutting, mitering, fastening, countersinking nails, and filling openings to achieve a smooth, professional finish.

Door and Window Installation: Measures, cuts, fits, and installs door and window frames, casings, hinges, locks, and strike plates; uses levels and squares to ensure proper alignment; and adjusts doors and windows for proper fit, swing, operation, and locking.

Maintenance and Alterations: Performs maintenance, repair, and alteration work on siding, roofs, doors, windows, partitions, and existing structures; constructs additions, relocates doors and partitions, and measures, cuts, assembles, and installs shelving, bulletin boards, rough cabinets, signs, scaffolding, and other building components.

Masonry: Constructs, maintains, and repairs brick, block, and stone structures and surfaces; lays materials in straight, level rows, removes damaged sections, prepares openings for doors and windows, repairs partitions and walkways, and mixes and applies mortar as required.

Plastering and Finishing: Mixes, applies, repairs, and finishes plaster and stucco on walls and ceilings; installs, tapes, and textures drywall; and applies primer, paint, and epoxy coatings to achieve durable, smooth, and finished surfaces

Physical Effort: Carpentry workers stand for extended periods while operating machines such as bench planers, saws, and drill presses. The work requires considerable bending, kneeling, and stooping.

When at a job site, strenuous physical exertion is sometimes required when handling heavy and bulky materials such as sheets of plywood, framing members, and other building and construction materials. Use manual or portable power tools for extended periods in uncomfortable positions.

On-site work typically requires bending, stooping, crawling, and climbing on ladders, scaffolding, and rooftops. Workers may lift and move materials up to 50 pounds, unassisted, and occasionally lift or move heavier items with the assistance of lifting devices or other workers.

Working Conditions: Some work is performed in shop areas where the worker is exposed to moderate or high noise levels from operating machinery, sawdust in the air, glue fumes, and hazards associated with woodworking and related power equipment.

When working at job sites, workers may be exposed to weather conditions and the hazards of working on and around scaffolds and ladders. They are subject to cuts, bruises, and contusions. Carpentry workers may work in confined areas such as crawl spaces and attics which may be dusty and dirty.

They use protective devices such as ear plugs, safety glasses, respirators, and gloves.
